Having regard the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction — UNDRR, its platform for Europe and central Asia, and the Making Cities Resilient 2030 initiative, / Having regard to Sauli Niinistö’s Report “Safer Together: Strengthening Europe’s Civilian and Military Preparedness and Readiness”1a,

---

1a Niinistö, Sauli: Safer Together: Strengthening Europe’s Civilian and Military Preparedness and Readiness, 2024. / Having regard to the WHO One Health Initiative, / Having regard to the framework for action of the Cross-agency One Health Task Force, / Having regard to the UN Global Assessment Report on Disaster Risk Reduction, / Having regard to the European Scientific Advisory Board on Climate Change report on 'Strengthening resilience to climate change – Recommendations for an effective EU adaptation policy framework', / (1) In view of the significant increase in the numbers and severity of natural and human-induced hazards in recent years, the strengthening of cooperation in the field of civil protection at Union level is necessary to create a resilient Union with the capabilities required to anticipate and manage those risks and threats, independently of their nature of origin, to ensure that the citizens of the Union enjoy adequate protection. The Union Civil Protection Mechanism (the ‘Union Mechanism’) should fulfil this role by strengthening cooperation and coordination among Member States to enhance the overall ability to anticipate, prevent, prepare for, respond to and enhance readiness to recover from disasters and crises. Due to the accelerating, interacting and cumulative nature of crises and health threats, prevention measures should be prioritised in order to reduce vulnerabilities, limit the number and severity of future crises and emergencies, and support readiness to recover. Preparedness measures, including capacity building, health preparedness and strengthening the resilience of Member States, should also be reinforced. The addition of new tasks and objectives should not negatively impact the tasks currently performed under the Union Mechanism. / (3) Prevention and preparedness measures are essential to enhance the resilience of the Union in facing natural and human-induced disasters. At the same time, the occurrence, timing and magnitude of disasters are by nature unpredictable. Therefore, financial resources required to ensure an adequate and effective response can vary significantly from year to year and should be made available immediately. Reconciling the budgetary principle of predictability with the necessity to react rapidly to new needs therefore means having to adapt the financial implementation of the work programmes. Consequently, it is appropriate to authorise carry-over of unused appropriations, limited to the following year and solely devoted to response actions, in addition to the carry-over of appropriations authorised under Article 12(4) of Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509 of the European Parliament and of the Council1a (the ‘Financial Regulation’). In order to allow for effective access to and mobilisation of Union support, particular attention should be paid to ensuring clarity, coherence and predictability of funding
